thesis: The program is a theory of observation and of the price of a distinction an observer cannot make: an observer sends states to records; its boundary is the set of merged pairs, two distinct states with one record; a target is determined by the record exactly when it is constant on each fiber, and this one criterion is statistical sufficiency, determinacy of a query by a view, a functional dependency, Padoa's method and Witsenhausen's confusable pairs. At a merged pair no reading the record determines separates the states, every protocol of such readings acquires zero information at every horizon, and the cost of resolving a pair grows like one over its discrimination; one side symbol the record does not carry resolves it, the least such alphabet is the largest fiber, and the resolving coordinates form one orbit under the permutations the record cannot see. The program realizes this boundary on two axes of one counted recursion, recur b s (succ n) → wrap s (recur b s n), the rule that copies its step argument and consumes one counter. On the termination axis the observer is a termination measure: the direct measures that read the copied payload cannot orient the step, a measure of the direct grammar orients it exactly when it ignores the payload and increases strictly with the counter, and the proofs that succeed change the observer, by the dependency-pair projection to the counter, by a nonlinear coupling or by a path order; seventy-six methods receive a machine-checked verdict, polynomial orientation is decided at unit slope, and the projected pair has ordinal height ω. On the confluence axis the observer is the content of a term: the equality test eqW a a of the calculus merges two copies that differ only in place, the reflexive diagonal is the one root obstruction to confluence, the disequality guard that repairs it is the greatest conservative repair and is definable by no term of the signature, the guarded relation terminates and has unique normal forms, and unique normal forms in general live in the normalizing core without termination; the published proof of Problem 79 fails at Lemma 64 of Kahrs and Smith, on a three-term counterexample, because its induction asserts a decrease across a step that reuses a piece. Gödel's sentence and its negation, Rice's theorem, perfect secrecy and the counted pass are instances of the same boundary, and the benchmark paper measures it in thirty language models, with the projection method recognized from a menu by ninety-four percent and constructed unaided in under one percent of the proofs. The Concrete Witness System, seven constructors and eight rules under the Lean name KO7, is the instrument: one small auditable calculus that carries both axes of fracture and their repairs, exported to TPDB and certified by TTT2 and CeTA, and every numbered claim of the papers has its Lean declarations in this repository.

theories.name: Release Assembly TPDB Export
theories.description: Assembles the full release for a single kernel check and renders TPDB texts. If main returns 0, both exporters match embedded literals and on-disk artifacts.
theories.oneLine: If the verifier main returns 0, both TPDB exporters match their embedded literals and on-disk artifacts.
theories.boundary: This theory asserts no separating boundary between provable and unprovable export properties. It certifies reproduction of TPDB texts across renderers, embedded literals and artifact copies. The divide it manages is between inside-Lean rendering and on-disk comparison, with the latter left to comparison outside Lean and discharged by the verifier executable.

theories.name: Confluence and Normalization of the Guarded Kernel Fragment
theories.description: Studies guarded SafeStep root and context closures. Every safe-fragment source is locally joinable and confluent with unique normal forms, while full Step fails at eqW void void.
theories.oneLine: Every guarded SafeStep source is locally joinable and confluent with unique normal forms, while full Step fails local joinability at eqW void void.
theories.boundary: On the guarded SafeStep side every source is locally joinable and the root and context closures are confluent with unique normal forms. On the full Step side this fails at eqW void void, where the eqW reflexive and difference rules overlap to give distinct normal-form reducts, contextually void and integrate void. The obstruction is this diagonal eqW overlap, located by the theorems denying LocalJoinStep at eqW void void and denying local confluence, confluence and invariant normalization for the full context closure while affirming them for SafeStep.

theories.name: Complexity Ordinal Trace Bounds
theories.description: Bounds guarded derivation lengths and trace images by ordinals below epsilon-zero. Contextual chains are single-exponential and DM triple-lex codes reach omega-omega times two, with recursor mass profiles exactly computed.
theories.oneLine: Guarded contextual derivations are single-exponentially bounded and their DM triple-lex ordinal codes have order type omega-omega times two below epsilon-zero with recursor mass profiles given by closed formulas.
theories.boundary: Guarded SafeStep strictly lowers the computable triple measure and its ordinal code below omega-omega times two under epsilon-zero, giving a well-founded reverse with linear root and single-exponential contextual envelopes, while the same root code rises on an exhibited contextual step under integrate so no universal root drop certifies full contexts and the bound must package fuel separately. The obstruction is marked by a concrete source-target pair with rising triple-lex measure, a payload-recursive family defeating every monotone arithmetic and lexicographic stack over four candidate coordinates, and a duplicating recursor with no direct additive whole-term witness although imported-whole and transformed-call witnesses remain. The location is fixed by bidirectional DM and triple-lex correspondences with upper bounds and surjectivity at omega-omega and omega-omega times two, cofinal tower families in both blocks, and a factor-two calibration separating matching from nonmatching mass profiles together with non-surjectivity and collision limits on the full carrier.

theories.name: Dependency Pairs and Estimated Dependency Graphs
theories.description: Extracts finite KO7 call graphs and proves termination by well-founded dependency pairs. TCAP estimation over-approximates the real graph and internal replay inherits well-foundedness.
theories.oneLine: Every KO7 dependency pair strictly decreases a counter-depth rank so the reverse pair relation is well-founded, and every real DP edge is covered by its TCAP estimate.
theories.boundary: By definition a measure orients the dependency-pair relation if it strictly drops along every pair, and then it drops along every SCC path by transitivity; an SCC pair with m source ≤ m target refutes orientation. On KO7 only R_rec_succ extracts a pair, the single pair decreases the counter rank dpRank and the linear counterHeight, and the reverse pair relation is well founded, so no barrier holds for natural-number orientations of the pair problem. TCAP estimation over-approximates real edges for every first-order system, so an absent estimated edge certifies an absent real edge; the replay record of the external certificate reuses the internal pair problem and records its indices.

theories.name: Direct Orientation Barrier Obstructions
theories.description: Shows no direct additive, affine, or pumped measure globally orients the duplicating step. All listed tool fragments fail globally while context closures lift the barriers.
theories.oneLine: No direct additive, affine, or pumped measure globally orients the duplicating step, while context closure preserves the failures and cross-coupled weights delimit the dominance hypotheses.
theories.boundary: A payload-reading direct measure rises on the pumped wrapper chain past a threshold already attained by a recursor term, so strict decrease across the duplicating step is impossible. The obstruction is the attained threshold and unbounded wrapper growth, while the payload-blind counter projection that forgets wrapper mass does decrease and does orient. The barrier is located by threshold, pump-discharge and certificate theorems that turn each measure with stated unboundedness, pump, dominance or positivity hypothesis into a concrete triple refuting global orientation, with ordered-field, grammar and dominance-sharpness results marking where the hypotheses are needed.

theories.name: Matrix, Arctic and Tropical Interpretations of a Duplicating Rule
theories.description: Rules out tracked matrix, arctic and tropical orientations under pumps and unboundedness. No fixed-row, row-sum or lexicographic matrix measure globally orients KO7.
theories.oneLine: No pumped or unbounded tracked, fixed-row, row-sum, lexicographic, arctic-primary or tropical matrix measure globally orients KO7, while tropical root orientation never lifts to wrapper contexts.
theories.boundary: On one side, pumped or unbounded interpretations cannot orient the duplicating step: wrapper gain dominates the pumped branch, so strict tracked decrease would force a strict natural increase already ruled out by the scalar barrier. The obstruction is the duplicating wrap-versus-recur step together with unbounded range, successor drift of at least one, wrapper drift of at least one, or positive wrapper diagonals. On the other side, bounded behavior, zero or bot diagonals, and one-sided wrapper policies escape: a bot-right arctic measure and a tropical escape measure orient root steps, while full wrapper-context closure remains impossible for every tropical measure.

theories.name: Path-Order and Polynomial Termination of the Kernel
theories.description: Proves termination by LPO, MPO below phi7 and nonlinear polynomial W, while KBO variable conditions, WPO polynomial orders and Yamada tuples cannot orient the duplicating step.
theories.oneLine: The KO7 kernel terminates by lexicographic path order, multiset path order below φ₇(0), and a nonlinear polynomial interpretation, while variable-condition KBO, bounded-polynomial and WPO-polynomial orders, and affine Yamada tuples cannot orient the duplicating recursor-successor step.
theories.boundary: On one side, the lexicographic path order, the fixed-precedence multiset path order and the nonlinear Wa and W with offset at least one strictly decrease along every root step, giving well-founded reverse reduction with ordinal ranks below φ₇(0). On the other side, any comparator satisfying the standard or weighted variable condition, any bounded polynomial or WPO-direct order with unbounded range plus frozen base dominance, any Yamada affine or additive-sum tuple, and MPO with app above recΔ cannot orient the duplicating step. The obstruction is the duplicated payload whose count rises from one to two: weighted s-count strictly rises and the frozen target dominates the source, located by the schema dupSrc and dupTgt theorems and their trace instantiations and by the smallest rec-succ counterexample.

theories.name: Projection-Rank Termination Methods and Their Universal Move
theories.description: Packages four licensed confession routes sharing one DP rank and forgetting witness. All routes converge to one core and the fifth usable-rules route closes with explicit transport.
theories.oneLine: Four distinctly licensed confession methods share one dependency-pair rank and converge to one core whose universal move carries a fifth usable-rules route closed by explicit transport.
theories.boundary: On the licensed transformed-call side every method orients the duplicating step downward and all four share one rank and one common route evidence. On the direct side no method is strictly sensitive to wrapper payload in either position, and rank agreement alone does not supply dependency-pair-to-source transport. The obstruction is the missing transport, recorded as open diagnostics for narrower attempts and discharged by the independent polynomial bridge that closes the fifth route; future admission is governed by the four equalities.

theories.name: Catalog of Termination Proof Routes and Six-Stage Ascent Profiles
theories.description: Classifies W1 licensed escapes, FBI catalogs and generic DP methods with six-step ascent profiles. Six canonical witnesses partition into W1 and W2 with permitted imports.
theories.oneLine: Six named construction packages are assigned by definition four to W1 imports and two to W2 transformed calls, and each carries proved evidence: the multiset path order and a polynomial interpretation orient the KO7 step, the full-duplicating benchmark member has a decreasing rank and no additive measure, and the dependency-pair projection decreases across the duplicating rule.
theories.boundary: For the benchmark recursion family a direct W0 route is an additive measure, and the full-duplicating member has none while it has a decreasing natural-number rank and a decreasing rank on transformed calls; for KO7, no orienter from the representable direct barrier classes orients the root relation, while the multiset path order and a non-transparent, non-affine polynomial interpretation do. The imported-whole and transformed-call levels of the tower ko7Tower carry the well-foundedness of the KO7 root relation and of the dependency-pair relation, and the benchmark contract holds at the transformed-call level because its definition excludes the two lower levels. Catalog closure statuses, the W1 classification of semantic methods and the MAYBE status of the external TTT2 run are recorded labels, and comparison maps between ascent profiles exist at the shape layer while the orientation and quotation ascents admit no ascent homomorphism either way.

theories.name: Escape Routes from Direct-Measure Barriers for Duplicating Recursion
theories.description: Shows every successful orienter lies outside enumerated universes via the third disjunct. Every duplicating family admits one-way classification and three exact escape routes.
theories.oneLine: Every direct orienter of the KO7 root relation fails wrapper-subterm sensitivity, base transparency or membership in the enumerated barrier universes, and in fact leaves those universes; every observer that orients a duplicating recursive family fails strict exposure, unbounded pump, visibility or sensitivity at each payload coordinate; and every KO7 orienter lands in one of three escape routes.
theories.boundary: Inside the enumerated direct-barrier universes no measure globally orients the KO7 duplicating step, so a global orientation gives up wrapper-subterm sensitivity, base transparency or representability, and the universe splits into disjoint scalar and structural halves, each without an orienter. For a duplicating recursive family the distinguished payload count rises strictly with gap at least one, and an orienting observer escapes by failure of exposure, pump, visibility or sensitivity; the implication runs one way, from orientation to escape. The schema-level outside-boundary theorem concerns KO7 recursor orbits under uniform-cost direct measures and makes no use of the schema.

theories.name: Diagonal Distinction Repair Boundary
theories.description: Isolates the eqW reflexive diagonal as the unique root confluence obstruction. Fork3 is minimal with one-bit collapse and guarded repairs restore confluence.
theories.oneLine: The reflexive eqW diagonal is the unique root confluence obstruction, minimally realized by the three-state Fork3 with a one-bit collapse repaired by disequality-guarded relations.
theories.boundary: Off the diagonal, Step is locally joinable and the difference branch is licensed by a ≠ b; on the diagonal eqW a a, void and integrate (merge a a) admit no common StepStar reduct so local join fails. The two-edge Fork3 peak marks this obstruction, and the completeness result locates root failure at IsEqWDiagonal. Guarded repairs restore confluence at the root and under frozen eqW with persistent disequality, but unrestricted context closure lets a licensed guard become diagonal and breaks confluence again.

theories.name: Boundary Observation Discrimination Protocols
theories.description: Characterizes merged pairs by zero discrimination and infinite reading costs for positive information. Finite observers and protocols obey exact cost bounds.
theories.oneLine: Merged pairs are exactly those with zero discrimination for every record-determined reading and zero information at infinite cost for any positive target.
theories.boundary: On the split side distinct records give positive triangular discrimination and one bit is recovered at unit cost, while on the merged side every record-determined reading has zero discrimination and every record-determined protocol has zero terminal and limit information. The obstruction is record-determinedness, kernel invisibility, nested supports or zero bias, which forces zero rows, zero gain and divergent price for any positive target. The results boundary_iff_blind, boundary_iff_infinite_cost and the three-descriptions equivalences locate the boundary exactly at merged pairs.

theories.name: Hartley Overproduction Gap Under Echo and Resolving Evidence
theories.description: Studies echo states with zero deficit and the one-bit Fork3 overproduction gap. Omega is nonnegative exactly when licensed bits do not exceed Hartley entropy, with optimal stopping cutoffs.
theories.oneLine: An echo channel leaves a gap equal to the full terminal Hartley entropy, giving a one-bit Fork3 overproduction gap that resolving evidence closes, while Omega stays nonnegative for capacity-compatible channels and stopping becomes optimal past marginal-price cutoffs.
theories.boundary: On the echo and zero-gain side the licensed bits fall short of the terminal Hartley envelope, so Omega is positive and a boundary event holds when strict branching with at least two reachable terminals is present. On the confluent and resolving side the licensed bits meet or exceed the envelope, so Omega is zero or negative with no boundary event, and the obstruction marking the crossing is whether a licensed channel supplies information about the target beyond the direct surface. The crossing is located by the order laws linking nonnegativity to capacity compatibility and boundary events to licensed bits below Hartley, with Fork3 echo at Omega one and resolving or licensed Fork3 at Omega zero as the concrete one-bit instance.

theories.name: Licensed Boundary Calculus Transactions
theories.description: Builds partial licensed morphisms, factorization and quantitative defect profiles. Composed transactions concatenate traces with additive ledgers and no universal semantic composer exists.
theories.oneLine: Partial licensed morphisms compose with five-factor factorization and additive trace ledgers, while semantic profiles require supplied composite data and admit no universal composer.
theories.boundary: Admitted in-domain edges compose and count additively on the licensed side, while out-of-domain states and rejected edges form disjoint additive defects that block totalization and surjectivity. Quotient-image dynamics forward-simulate always but agree with image steps on the lifting side and diverge on the non-lifting side, marked by an image self-step with no quotient edge. Semantic profiles follow the morphism-trace pair on the supplied-capability side and separate from it on the other side, where one identity composite admits two adequate decorations with different costs and one morphism-trace pair carries two profiles, so no factor-only rule recovers all composites.

theories.name: Operational Inexpressibility License Theory
theories.description: Proves fixed-input languages cannot derive termination verdicts though licensed channels separate systems. Fourteen declared profiles agree yet the verdict distinguishes them.
theories.oneLine: Fixed-input observation-only languages cannot decide global termination on a shared trace input where fourteen declared profiles coincide, while a proof-backed licensed channel separates the systems.
theories.boundary: On the licensed side an observer augmented with distinguishing side information factors the target and the certificate channel separates recursor from self-embedding with zero residual. On the direct side derivable observation-only statements are constant on observer fibers and the fourteen-profile observation coincides, so no derivable statement constrains or decides termination. The obstruction is an explicit colliding pair with equal observations and distinct targets at fixed input and shared context. The results locating it are the profile-equality plus collision and no-decoder theorems together with the licensed-separation headline carrying log-2 deficit.

theories.name: Godel Reverse Mathematics Calibration
theories.description: Formalizes Godel numbering, incompleteness and RCA0-style calibration at WO omega-cubed below epsilon-zero. The Godel sentence is true exactly when unprovable and ConQ is independent.
theories.oneLine: The Godel sentence holds in the standard model exactly when it is unprovable, so neither it nor its negation is provable and consistency is independent.
theories.boundary: The boundary is provability in the Robinson-Q checker versus truth in the standard model: every checked proof is true in every model of the axioms, yet the Godel sentence is true exactly when unprovable and consistency is true in the standard model but false in the one-infinite-element model, so neither the Godel sentence nor consistency is decided by the checker. The obstruction is the diagonal fixed point together with the beta-coded proof relation, which lets truth and provability separate and blocks any total recoding bridge across all conclusion codes. The calibration side locates the same divide at RCA0 plus well-ordering of omega-cubed strictly below epsilon-zero, where the recorded target, order and absence of matching bounds hold with conjectural status and sharp exactness holds only with supplied target-matching theories, ordinals and theorem-level evidence.

theories.name: Six-Slot External-License Extension Schemas and Their Comparison Maps
theories.description: Packages six-slot LCEL instances with base, license and reimport supports. Godel, benchmark and DP instances are pairwise stagewise equivalent with universal quasi-functors.
theories.oneLine: Godel, benchmark-transport and DP-emitter six-slot instances compare by stagewise equivalence with universal quasi-functors when explicit comparison, admissibility and bridge witnesses are supplied.
theories.boundary: With per-side realization together with a cross-instance mathematical witness, or admissibility data with a pairwise bridge and canonical transport equalities, universal quasi-functors with target packages exist between admissible instances on the original carriers. With realization alone, or with constant target-returning maps, comparison collapses to subsingleton biconditionals built from stored inhabitants, classifying by truth values while failing to transport stage witnesses. The missing witness, blueprint and coherence data mark the divide, located by the equivalence between admission and the three Nonempty components and by the result that an inhabited certified catalog still requires universal certification and blueprints.

theories.name: Unique Normalization Rewriting Diagrams
theories.description: Develops first-order rewriting, decreasing diagrams and conditional linearizations for unique normal forms. Down is a consistency invariant and KO7 lies outside with a printed Lemma 64 counterexample.
theories.oneLine: First-order rewriting with conditional hub linearizations and decreasing diagrams yields unique normal forms under non-omega-overlap and variable conditions, while Down stays a consistency invariant and the printed Lemma 64 promotion with KO7 lies outside.
theories.boundary: On one side Down and DownOn are least closed consistency invariants that absorb rewriting and support Horn and finite-table computation, and complete targeted graphs can be universal when root steps are represented. On the other side the three-node d(x) to x carrier satisfies the consistency invariant, targeting and completeness yet fails universality because the bar of Down relates once and twice while the bar of graph equality does not. The obstruction is the missing root representation together with non-joinable KO7 and Huet peaks, and the counterexample to Lemma 64 as printed marks the dividing line for promotion from Down arguments to graph equality.

theories.name: Sharing-Sensitive Counters and Capture Avoidance in Higher-Order Rewriting
theories.description: Shows shared-policy counters orient embedded beta steps while tree barriers do not lift unqualified. Full capture is blocked with decidable capture checks and an eight-row closeout catalog.
theories.oneLine: A counter reading only the argument branch of an application under the shared policy, and one reading only the continuation of a share node under explicit sharing, orient the duplicating recursor step, refuting any lift of the tree barrier to every policy; no direct measure orients duplicating beta, the beta-compatible counter fails on a beta step, and capture avoidance fails without freshness of the binder in the body and holds with it, with exact decidable gates on the binder-free, share-free fragment.
theories.boundary: Under the shared and explicit-sharing policies every duplicating and rewrite step strictly decreases the policy counter, so the claim that no policy admits an orienting counter is false; the files of this theory prove no nonorientation theorem for the tree policy, which enters only through that refuted lift. Duplicating beta resists every direct measure, with the variable-constant case reduced to the threshold 2c, and the beta-compatible counter fails on an explicit beta step. Capture avoidance fails without freshness of the binder in the body and holds with it, and the closeout marks full higher-order rewriting as outside, so the blocked rows give no unrestricted impossibility.

theories.name: Finite Channels, Fisher Information and Cramér-Rao Bounds
theories.description: Builds finite stochastic channels, distributions and parametric families, proves Fisher data processing under a fixed Markov kernel and the finite Cramér-Rao bound for locally unbiased estimators, and gives the sharp quadratic lower bound on binary entropy.
theories.oneLine: Finite Fisher information contracts under fixed Markov kernels and lower-bounds unbiased estimator variance, while binary entropy admits a sharp quadratic lower bound.
theories.boundary: On the informative side a fixed kernel carrying both probability and tangent pushforwards never raises Fisher information and the drop equals the mean squared score residual, with equality holding if and only if input scores are preserved on every possible output. On the other side probability transfer alone can raise Fisher, zero-Fisher constant families admit no positive-Fisher division for the variance floor, and constant-one tangents and mass above one are impossible. The contraction theorem, its score-preservation equivalences, the variance bound with its outside cases, and the sharp entropy lower bound with recorded tightness at one half locate the boundary.

theories.name: Uniform Inversion, Positive Binary Quadratic Forms and Hermitian Kernels
theories.description: Proves compact-uniform reciprocal convergence, critical-circle modulus from positivity, and positive-semidefinite Gram realizations for based Hermitian kernels.
theories.oneLine: On an open set, a family compact-uniformly separated from zero and converging locally uniformly has reciprocals converging locally uniformly; nonnegativity of x^2 + a*x*y + q*y^2 at all integer vectors is equivalent to a^2 <= 4*q and gives every zero of X^2 - a*X + q modulus sqrt q; and every finite Gram matrix of a based Hermitian kernel is positive semidefinite and realized by Euclidean feature vectors.
theories.boundary: On an open set, compact-uniform separation from zero is a sufficient condition for pointwise inversion to preserve locally uniform convergence; the reciprocal theorems prove sufficiency only. The family 1/(n+1) is nonzero at every point and fails compact-uniform separation on the whole plane, so pointwise nonvanishing does not give the separation hypothesis. For the quadratic form, nonnegativity at all real vectors, equivalently at all integer vectors, holds exactly when a^2 <= 4*q, and on that side the factorization through the explicit roots and the root-modulus theorems place every zero of X^2 - a*X + q on the circle of radius sqrt q.

theories.name: Orientation Closure Method Rows
theories.description: Closes 76 method families with native witnesses on the free recursor. Orientation is exactly payload blindness plus strict counter response with exact hypothesis necessity.
theories.oneLine: A reflected expression orients the duplicating successor on the free recursor if and only if it is payload-blind with strict counter response, and all 76 method families close with native witnesses.
theories.boundary: On the orienting side, payload-blind counter-strict measures decrease from wrapped recursive call to successor instance at every carrier. On the failing side, payload-reading or counter-non-strict measures admit a concrete failed instance, and barrier-cell measures with unbounded wrapper cost and bounded gain admit no uniform orientation. The obstruction is the payload count growing from one to two with wrapper cost outrunning counter gain, located by the set equality between orienters and payload-blind counter-strict expressions together with the barrier-cell exclusion.

theories.name: RDRS Termination Method Atlas
theories.description: Enumerates 76 method families with total classification into barrier, escape and licensed statuses. Twelve semantic rows and fourteen algebraic rows close with exact mechanisms.
theories.oneLine: The 76-method universe is fully classified into barrier, escape and licensed statuses with closed algebraic, path-order, semantic and coverage layers.
theories.boundary: Direct payload-sensitive orientation holds on the escape side through projection transactions that transport a well-founded projected orientation back through a commuting projection with seed-collapse and counter factoring, and it fails on the barrier side where lens-pump witnesses, KBO variable-count obstructions and duplication gaps refute orientation. The obstruction is a single triple where the strict order fails, a pump violation, or a payload-erasure that forces every orienting measure to be counter-dominated. The location is recorded by the universe closure and ledger closures that place 28 families in payload-sensitive blocked, 8 in projection escape and the remainder in construction, transform and not-direct buckets, with W0 witnesses boundary-blocked and W2 witnesses admissible.

theories.name: Nonlinear Direct Measures and the Residual Method Catalog
theories.description: Classifies seven nonlinear residual families with dominance data blocking orientation. The 25-row inventory is terminally classified but not universally closed.
theories.oneLine: Every nonlinear residual family carries its row-specific support and the twenty-five-row inventory is terminally classified without being universally closed.
theories.boundary: With eventual base dominance or a member of the concrete dominance class supplied, a transparent bounded polynomial with unbounded range cannot globally orient; without that data the boundary keeps the recorded status projection-required. A direct law that keeps both wrapper arguments and bounds the counter gain cannot orient the duplicating step, and on free terms dropping either clause admits an orienter. The twenty-five-row certificate gives every row support and a terminal recorded status, and the recorded blocked and licensed-escape rows make the inventory not universally closed; the arbitrary-relation dichotomy is complete only because its carrier admits the kernel relation alone.

theories.name: Termination Barriers for Mutually Recursive Duplicating Cycles
theories.description: Shows finite cyclic delayed-duplication systems admit no additive or unbounded-affine orientation. Every bounded cycle realizes its path with executable search sound and complete.
theories.oneLine: Every finite cyclic delayed-duplication system realizes its one-cycle path by transitive closure yet admits no additive and, when the derived one-cycle witness is unbounded, no affine global orientation, with executable cycle search sound and complete.
theories.boundary: On the realization side every bounded finite cycle with certified successor steps reaches its wrapped target by transitive closure of the contextual relation, while on the orientation side no additive measure and no unbounded affine measure can decrease along all those steps. The obstruction is the realized one-cycle composite itself, which forces any candidate measure to rise from source to target: additive pumps always rise, affine pumps rise when the derived one-cycle witness is unbounded, and wrapper dominance or transparency marks the same limit in preserving variants. The finite-cycle no-go theorems, their final-catalog projections and the packet-cycle non-well-foundedness locate this boundary, while executable search succeeds on the realizable side and reports a missing edge on the failure side.

theories.name: Universal Boundary Primitive Capacity
theories.description: States true verdicts are not functions of cheap observations. No payload-monotone measure orients the step and message cardinality does not exceed key cardinality.
theories.oneLine: True verdicts are not functions of cheap observations.
theories.boundary: On one side a cheap observation collides on two states while the true verdict differs, so no function of that observation alone returns the verdict and an added licensing channel is needed. The obstruction is the colliding pair with equal observations and unequal verdicts, which blocks observation-only rules, orientation by a measure with an unbounded section, ciphertext-only licensing under perfect secrecy, and joint availability-consistency and agreement-validity-silence requirements. The universal verdict-not-function theorem locates this limit, and the Shannon message-at-most-key bound with Hamming, syndrome, compression, sorting, Byzantine, partition, gradual, timing and two-generals collisions instantiate it.

programs.name: The Observation Boundary
programs.summary: An observer sends states to records, and its boundary is the set of merged pairs: two distinct states with one record, told apart by no record-determined reading, at infinite resolution cost, repaired by one side symbol whose least alphabet is the largest fiber. The license criterion, under which a target is determined exactly when it is constant on the fibers, is proved on arbitrary sets with its lattice, its Bayes-risk and Blackwell comparison, its Beth gap, the echo law and Shannon's secrecy bound.

programs.name: The Termination Axis
programs.summary: The rule recΔ b s (δ n) → app s (recΔ b s n) copies its payload and consumes one counter; a direct measure orients it exactly when it ignores the payload and increases strictly with the counter, and the additive, affine, matrix, arctic, tropical and Knuth-Bendix families fail under their stated premises, with mutual cycles and higher-order sharing as variants. The proofs that succeed change the observer: the dependency-pair projection to the counter, nonlinear coupling, and the lexicographic and multiset path orders; seventy-six methods and a residual catalog record the verdicts as bookkeeping.

programs.name: The Confluence Axis
programs.summary: The equality test eqW merges two copies of one term that differ only in place: the reflexive diagonal is the one root obstruction to confluence, the disequality guard that repairs it is the greatest conservative repair and is definable by no term of the signature, and the guarded relation terminates and has unique normal forms while the unguarded closure gives eqW void void two normal forms. For first-order rewriting, non-omega-overlap with right-hand-side determinedness gives unique normal forms under the Section 7 hypothesis of Kahrs and Smith, and a three-term counterexample refutes their Lemma 64, the step the published proof of Problem 79 rests on.

programs.name: Certificates and Confession
programs.summary: A construction method adds comparison data and verifies the original relation; a confession method transforms the problem, omits a coordinate and transports the result through a soundness theorem. The confession routes for the kernel share the canonical dependency-pair rank, the typed external-license schemas are related by quasi-functors with one irreversible license stage, and licensed transactions compose with ledgers while no rule recovers the composite semantic profile from the factor capabilities alone.

programs.name: Ordinals and Reverse Mathematics
programs.summary: Guarded contextual derivations have single-exponential length with a matching lower family, the Dershowitz-Manna codes have order type ω^ω, the calibrated triple codes stay below ω^ω·2, and the projected dependency pair has height ω. The compiled Robinson-Q checker satisfies both incompleteness theorems, so Gödel's sentence and its negation share one provability record, and the size-change calibration enters as a recorded profile over a proved ω³ well-ordering.

programs.name: Statistical and Analytic Instances
programs.summary: The statistics results build finite stochastic channels and parametric families, prove Fisher data processing under a fixed Markov kernel and the finite Cramér-Rao bound, and give the sharp quadratic bound on binary entropy. The analytic results give positivity of integer binary quadratic forms, uniform inversion under compact separation and Hermitian kernel realizations.

programs.name: The Instrument: TPDB Export
programs.summary: The Concrete Witness System, seven constructors and eight rules under the Lean name KO7, is the calculus that carries both axes inside one auditable signature. Its TPDB text rendered from the rule patterns equals the embedded artifact copy, parses back to the declared rules, and is the object TTT2 and CeTA certify.

relations.statement: Orientation method rows build on first-order rewriting terms and substitutions.
Complexity bounds build on Trace and fuel measures for safe steps.
Scalar grammar classifiers build on direct measure evaluations.
Matrix barrier proofs build on duplicating schema iterators.
Path-order native semantics build on symbolic comparator terms.
Orientation witnesses build on free schema and free terms.

The root characterization proves that full Step has a non-joinable one-step peak at a source if and only if the source is a diagonal eqW c c, generalizing the single non-joinable source eqW void void of the kernel confluence theory.
The contextual nonconfluence and two-normal-form theorems for StepCtxFull use the closure CtxStar and the non-joinability of the eqW void void peak from the contextual diagonal scope.
The tool-search coverage status catalog records the matrix residual closure status.
The closed native-coverage record is indexed by the 76 RDRS method families.
Newman's lemma for SafeStep takes its termination premise from the well-foundedness of reverse SafeStep, proved by the decrease of the computable triple measure on every guarded step.
The dependency-pair confession route takes its evidence from the pair relation extracted from rec_succ, its counter rank dpRank and the well-foundedness of the reverse pair relation.
The additive barrier applies to the kernel: no additive compositional measure on Trace orients every instance of recΔ b s (delta n) → app s (recΔ b s n), so none orients every rule of Step.
The unbounded-range affine barrier for one duplicating step extends to the composite step of a mutual duplication cycle.
The positive termination verdict for the KO7 root step in the inexpressibility theorem is the well-foundedness of reverse Step proved by the nonlinear polynomial interpretation.
The metric diagonal grade D1u is proved equivalent to compact-uniform separation from zero, and the reciprocal convergence theorem for that separation transfers to D1u.

path.statement: For two distinct states, the records are equal if and only if every record-determined adaptive protocol acquires zero information at every horizon and in the limit, and if and only if every positive information target has infinite cost.
path.significance: The boundary of an observer is its set of merged pairs, and the merged pair is the unit of the whole program.

path.statement: An observer licenses a target if and only if a decoder on the attained image reads it, and the license fails if and only if a collision exists: two states with one record and two target values.
path.significance: The license criterion is statistical sufficiency, determinacy of a view, a functional dependency and Padoa's method in one statement.

path.statement: For reading rows of positive triangular discrimination Δ, every protocol with row discrimination at most Δ that reaches c bits at a horizon has expected cost at least c ln 2 / Δ.
path.significance: The resolution cost has a pole of order one at the boundary: a merged pair costs every finite budget.

path.statement: The largest fiber size is the least size of a side alphabet that resolves every merged pair, and its ceiling logarithm is the least fixed bit width, attained by an optimal channel.
path.significance: A side symbol the record does not carry is the repair, and its size is the fiber.

path.statement: An expression of the reflected direct grammar orients the duplicating step if and only if its value ignores the payload and increases strictly with the counter.
path.significance: The Orientation Boundary: one set of measures described twice, by the rewrite steps and by two conditions on the expression.

path.statement: A measure is payload-blind exactly when the counter observer licenses it, so every orienting grammar denotation is counter-licensed and the payload target collides.
path.significance: The termination axis is a license failure: the orienting measures read the counter record and nothing else.

path.statement: Over an ordered commutative semiring with the strict ordered-semiring laws, no affine measure with wrapper coefficients at least one orients the duplicating step.
path.significance: A barrier: a measure that keeps both wrapper arguments at a fixed cost and gains a bounded amount per counter step fails.

path.statement: The reverse of the dependency-pair relation extracted from the duplicating rule is well-founded, with no hypotheses.
path.significance: The first escape: the projection to the counter drops the copied payload and changes the observer.

path.statement: The transitive lexicographic path order with the CeTA precedence orients every full contextual step of the kernel.
path.significance: The second escape: a path order imports subterm structure from outside the direct grammar, and the whole kernel terminates.

path.statement: For every trace, the full root relation has a non-joinable one-step peak at the trace if and only if the trace is a reflexive equality test eqW c c.
path.significance: The confluence axis: the equality test merges two copies of one term that differ only in place, and that merged pair is the one root obstruction.

path.statement: No term over the seven constructors with two predicate-variable slots, and no such term with a fixed truth token, defines disequality on closed terms.
path.significance: The repair of the fork needs a side symbol: the guard comes from outside the signature.

path.statement: The guarded relation SafeStep has unique normal forms, with no hypotheses.
path.significance: Behind the guard the calculus is confluent with one normal form per term; the unguarded closure gives eqW void void two normal forms.

path.statement: The invariant can be a consistency invariant while a complete targeted proof graph is not universal, so the printed implication of Lemma 64 of Kahrs and Smith fails on a three-term carrier.
path.significance: The published proof of Problem 79 asserts a decrease across a step that reuses a piece; the program's method located the gap.

path.statement: The extracted dependency-pair step is well-founded, with pointwise rank equal to its counter and ordinal height ω.
path.significance: The projected pair is predecessor descent of height ω: the escape is calibrated.

path.statement: The TPDB text rendered from the eight rule patterns equals the embedded artifact copy.
path.significance: The instrument leaves the repository: the calculus that carries both axes is exported and certified by TTT2 and CeTA.

featured.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.SeedFrontier.seed_frontier
featured.statement:
theorem seed_frontier (c : ℝ) (hc0 : 0 ≤ c) (hc1 : c ≤ 1) :
    (∃ p : ConditionalProtocol Bool Bool Unit Bool,
      (∀ u z, p.initialJoint.mass (u, z) = p.initialRecord.mass u * binaryPrior (1 / 2) z) ∧
      (∀ u h a z y, ((p.given u).observation h a z).mass y = if y = z then 1 else 0) ∧
      (∀ u h a, (p.given u).cost h a = 1) ∧
      conditionalMI p 1 (historyBank Unit Bool 1) = c ∧
      conditionalExpectedCost p 1 (historyBank Unit Bool 1) = c) ∧
    (∀ (H0 Z A : Type) [Fintype H0] [Fintype Z] [Fintype A]
      (p : ConditionalProtocol H0 Z A Bool),
      (∀ u, 0 < p.initialRecord.mass u → ∀ h a, 1 ≤ (p.given u).cost h a) →
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (bank : List (List (A × Bool))), HistoryBank n bank →
        conditionalMI p n bank ≤ conditionalExpectedCost p n bank)

featured.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.StochasticGraph.repeated_conflictGraph_eq
featured.statement:
theorem repeated_conflictGraph_eq {X Y V : Type*} (K : X → Y → ℝ) (hK : ∀ x y, 0 ≤ K x y)
    (P : X → V) (N : ℕ) :
    conflictGraph (repeated K (N + 1)) P = conflictGraph K P

featured.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryInfiniteCost.boundary_iff_blind
featured.statement:
theorem boundary_iff_blind {X Q : Type} (q : X → Q) {x₀ x₁ : X} (hne : x₀ ≠ x₁) :
    IsMergedPair q x₀ x₁ ↔
      ∀ (A Y : Type) [Fintype A] [Fintype Y] (p : FiniteProtocol Bool A Y)
        (K : List (A × Y) → A → Reading X Y),
        (∀ h a, RecordDetermined q (K h a)) →
        (∀ h a b, p.observation h a b = K h a (pairState x₀ x₁ b)) →
        (∀ n bank, HistoryBank n bank → terminalMI p n bank = 0) ∧ informationLimit p = 0
